items.title: Water Minute · Why "free water tests" aren't really free
items.preview:
Words I like;
Free isn't free when the guy holding the test kit also holds a commission check.
Let me save you a headache. When a company knocks on your door offering a free in-home water test, understand what's happening. Most of those tests are theater. They drop a chemical in your glass, it turns purple or foamy, and suddenly you're staring at "proof" you need to buy something today.
Here's the truth. Real water testing gives you numbers. Hardness in grains per gallon. Iron in parts per million. pH. Chlorine. Nitrates if you're on a well. A drop that changes color tells you almost nothing except that a reaction happened. Any water does that. Even good water does that.
A trustworthy test tells you what's in your water and how much. Then it lets YOU decide, on your own time, with no pressure to sign before the guy leaves your kitchen.
If you already own a Re-Ionator Pro Ultra or an RO Pure PRO QC, this is exactly why you're set. You bought based on real numbers, not a color trick. That was a smart call, and your water proves it every single day.
On a well and unsure what's actually in your water? Reply and I'll send you our free water assessment.
As promised, value in under a minute.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave

items.title: Email Campaign · 1: Referral Push (30-60 Day Post-Install)
items.preview:
**Audience:** Referral push candidates, 30 members (satisfied, 30-60 days post-install)
This is your highest-conversion play. These clients just spent real money (several at $5K-$11K), the install glow is fresh, and referrals are cash-in-pocket rather than a review ask. No product-name landmines if we use the tenure line for legacy systems.
**Note on the list:** Several here have current ClearWave names I CAN use (Justin Houghton = SOVEREIGN, Jena Tomer = PINNACLE). Others hold legacy/mixed names (Jason Vallee, Elizabeth Simmeth) so those get the tenure line. Liz Gleason is "(not specified)" so gets "your ClearWave system."
### Subject Lines (pick 1, 4 alternates)
- **Primary (specific):** `Your water is dialed in. Now here's $500.`
- Curiosity: `The thing our best clients do around day 45`
- Pain: `Know someone still living with their water?`
- Authority: `Why ClearWave grows almost entirely by word of mouth`
- Specific: `$500 per referral (and it climbs from there)`
### Preview Text
`No review needed. Just introduce us to someone who needs better water.`
### Email Body (template with two example merges shown)
**Version A (current-name client, e.g. Justin Houghton / SOVEREIGN):**
> Hi Justin,
>
> It's been about a month since we installed your ClearWave SOVEREIGN, and by now the water has settled into what it should be: clean, consistent, the way it was engineered to be.
>
> Here's the honest truth about how we grow. We don't run loud campaigns. Most of our new clients come from someone exactly like you making one introduction.
>
> So here's the offer, and the numbers are real:
>
> - A referral who becomes a client: **$500 cash** (referrals 1 through 5 this year)
> - It climbs to **$750** for 6 through 9, and **$1,000** at 10 or more
> - Even a referral who just books a consult and doesn't move forward: **$50 gift card**
>
> All they get is a free water assessment. No pressure, no hard sell. If you know a neighbor, a family member, or a coworker who's tired of their water, just reply with their name and I'll take it from there.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
**Version B (legacy-name client, e.g. Jason Vallee):**
> Hi Jason,
>
> It's been about a month since we installed your water system, and by now it should be running exactly the way it was engineered to.
>
> Here's the honest truth about how we grow. We don't run loud campaigns. Most of our new clients come from someone exactly like you making one introduction.
>
> [same referral block + free water assessment close as above]
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
### Send Timing
**Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET** (highest B2C open window; avoids Monday inbox clog).
### Expected Performance
- **Open: 48-55%.** Small, warm, recently-engaged list. Well above 42% account avg because these people literally just interacted with your company. Non-salesy subject clears spam filters that are killing your discount blasts.
- **Click: 8-15%** (vs 0.28% avg). Reply-driven CTA plus concrete dollar amounts. The 0.28% avg is dragged down by dead cold sends; a warm 30-person list behaves completely differently.
- **Conversion: 3-6 referral introductions.** Even 1 closed referral = $500 cost against a client acquisition that's typically worth thousands.
### Source Justification
Draws from **JOBBER LIFECYCLE TRIGGERS → Referral push candidates (30-60 days post-install)** and the **REFERRAL BONUS STRUCTURE**. Honors Rule 3 (referrals, not reviews) and Rule 3a ("free water assessment").
---

items.title: Email Campaign · 2: Concierge "Is It Worth It?" (Year 1.5 Clients)
items.preview:
**Audience:** Concierge upsell candidates (13-24 months, not on Concierge), 100 members
This is a large, trust-established segment ($99/mo recurring revenue upside) that's already past year-1 service, so the hard floor (Rule 1) is cleared. Framed as honest math, not a pitch, which fits both the Concierge voice guidance and your deliverability recovery goal.
### Subject Lines
- **Primary (curiosity):** `The question we get at year 1.5`
- Pain: `Doing your own filter swaps? Read this first.`
- Authority: `Is Concierge actually worth it? Here's the math.`
- Specific: `$99/mo, and exactly what it covers`
- Curiosity: `We'll be honest about whether you need this`
### Preview Text
`No pressure. Just the real math on whether Concierge makes sense for your home.`
### Email Body (legacy-name example, e.g. Peggy Buelow)
> Hi Peggy,
>
> It's been a little over a year since we installed your water system, and if you're like most clients around this point, you've probably wondered: is this Concierge thing actually worth it for me?
>
> Fair question. Here's the honest math, no spin.
>
> Concierge is **$99/mo** and covers:
>
> - Your annual service, done for you
> - Filter swaps (no ordering, no guessing, no forgetting)
> - Priority phone support when you need a real person
> - Parts coverage on your standard install components
>
> If you're the type who'd rather handle swaps yourself and call us as needed, you may genuinely not need it. But if you'd rather never think about maintenance again and want the parts protection, it usually pays for the peace of mind.
>
> Want me to look at your specific system and tell you straight whether it makes sense? Just reply "math" and I'll send you the breakdown for your home.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(For current-name clients in this segment, swap the tenure line for "since we installed your ClearWave [CREST/MERIDIAN/etc.]." For "(not specified)" use "your ClearWave system.")*
### Send Timing
**Thursday, 11:00 AM ET** (mid-week, mid-morning; separated from Tuesday's referral send so no audience overlap fatigue).
### Expected Performance
- **Open: 40-46%.** Warm but slightly cooler than Proposal 1 (installs are 13-24 mo old). Curiosity subject with zero discount language should hold near account average.
- **Click/reply: 3-6%.** The low-friction "reply 'math'" CTA outperforms link clicks for this list and dodges click-tracking spam penalties.
- **Conversion: 2-5 Concierge signups.** At $99/mo, even 3 signups = ~$3,600/yr recurring. Strong ROI on one send.
### Source Justification
Draws from **JOBBER LIFECYCLE TRIGGERS → Concierge upsell candidates (13-24 months)** and **CONCIERGE UPSELL CONTEXT** (the "$99/mo," the "is it worth it at year 1.5" framing, the non-pushy math tone). Respects Rule 1 (list is pre-filtered past 12 months) and Rule 2 (tenure line for legacy names).
---
## Recommended Sequencing
Run **Proposal 1 Tuesday** (highest conversion, rebuilds sender reputation with a warm, engaged audience) and **Proposal 2 Thursday**. Zero audience overlap between the two. Both deliberately avoid the discount/salesy subject patterns that tanked your last five sends, which should also start repairing deliverability across the whole account.

---
